title: Partner portal listing playbook — marketplace copy & reqs
content:
Purpose
------
Working playbook + copy snippets + technical & legal checklist to onboard Redwood Inference into cloud partner portals (AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace, GCP Marketplace). This is a working doc — lightweight, intentionally informal. Use as single source for go-to-market + engineering handoffs for listings.

Goals for this doc
- Provide copy variants for short/long descriptions and feature bullets that satisfy marketplace style constraints.
- Capture per-cloud technical packaging requirements and owner for each task.
- Define asset checklist and approval flow (legal, security, pricing).
- Surface unresolved questions and decisions needed for final submission.

Audience
- GTM Partnerships, Product Marketing, Legal, Engineering (pkg & infra), Sales Ops, Solutions Eng.

Status & constraints
- Current status: draft copy + initial requirements gathered. Need legal review and final pricing SKU matrix.
- Deadline target for first marketplace submission (AWS SaaS): 2026-03-20 (aggressive).

High-level listing types we may target
- SaaS (hosted API via Redwood hosted infra; simplest for PLG + usage billing)
- Private Offer / Reserved Capacity (for Dedicated customers) — needs contract templates + entitlements mapping
- Bring-your-own-license (BYOL) / On-prem agent or AMI (for Private deployments) — requires image packaging and security attestations

Copy snippets (short -> 1 line, medium -> 1–2 sentences, long -> full paragraph):
Short (headline) variants
- "Low-latency LLM inference with predictable cost and enterprise controls"
- "Run production LLMs: fast, reliable, and cost-aware inference"

Medium (1–2 sentences) variants
- "Redwood Inference provides a developer-first platform for running LLM inference at production scale. Choose hosted, dedicated, or private deployments with built-in observability, fallbacks, and cost controls."
- "Ship LLM-powered features quickly: streaming responses, model versioning, and automated caching to reduce per-token cost while preserving latency SLAs."

Long description (marketplace-friendly)
- "Redwood Inference is a unified runtime for serving large language models across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We optimize for production economics — low latency, predictable unit cost, and robust rollouts. Built-in features include automatic KV/prefix caching, intelligent batching, model variant fallbacks, and a console for tracing, per-token cost breakdowns, and canary/A-B rollouts. Integrates with cloud IAM and KMS, and supports private VPC install for regulated workloads."

Feature bullets (short)
- "Multi-mode deployment: Hosted API, Dedicated GPU pools, Private VPC/on-prem"
- "Streaming responses, function/tool-calling, structured outputs"
- "Observability: per-model dashboards, tracing, and token-level cost"
- "Cost controls: batching, quantization recommendations, cache suggestions"

Suggested asset copy mapping (marketplace fields):
- Short summary -> Short headline variant 1 (or 2)
- Detailed summary -> Long description above
- Key features -> feature bullets (3–6 items max)
- Support contact -> partner-support@redwood.ai (placeholder)
- Logo -> 1200x1200 PNG (see assets checklist)

Per-cloud technical checklist (engineer owner listed)
1) AWS Marketplace (SaaS integration) — owner: Liam O'Connor
   - SaaS contract integration: configure AWS SaaS Integration (SaaS metering) and Listen/Notify endpoints
   - API usage metering: decide on meter type (usage-based tokens vs flat seat) -> action: proposal in REDW-3124
   - Entitlement testing: end-to-end entitlement flow with account mapping and Redshift/tenant mapping
   - Security docs: SOC2 summary + VPC network diagrams + KMS integration notes required by AWS
   - Endpoint SLAs mapping: document latency SLOs and fallback model behavior

2) Azure Marketplace (SaaS + Private Offers) — owner: Priya Singh
   - Publisher registration and MPN validation
   - Pricing model mapping and plan definitions for Azure Commerce
   - Azure AD SSO instructions for onboarding (SAML/OAuth) and API key mapping
   - ARM template/managed application packaging if offering private deployable artifacts

3) GCP Marketplace — owner: Diego Alvarez
   - Configure SaaS activation flow, entitlements via Pub/Sub callbacks
   - GCP IAM role recommendations and VPC-SC considerations for private installs
   - Prepare container images / GKE Marketplace listing notes for a BYOL option

Assets checklist (marketing + engineering)
- Logo files: 1200x1200 PNG (transparent), 512x512, and SVG source — owner: Design
- 3–5 screenshots: console model dashboard, tracing view, usage cost-breakdown — size: 1200x800 PNG
- Short demo video: 60–90s MP4 with captions (optional) — host on S3 with public token
- PDF product one-pager + architecture diagram (VPC/private deploy flow) — owner: Product
- Security artifacts: SOC2 summary, ISO/PCI statements if available, penetration test summary — owner: Security
- Pricing matrix CSV with SKU ids and billing metric definitions — owner: Finance

Pricing & SKU draft notes
- Proposed starter plan: "Developer" — pay-as-you-go tokens, no commitment, for self-serve onboarding
- "Dedicated" plan — monthly reserved GPU capacity with two commitment tiers (small/medium/large)
- Private deployments: licensing fee + per-node support (quote-based)
- Need finance to define marketplace SKU ids and map to Redwood billing realms -> action: Finance to propose by 2026-02-28

Approval flow (suggested)
1. GTM drafts copy + assets -> internal review in #gtm-marketplace (2 business days)
2. Legal review (TOS, marketplace agreements) -> legal@redwood.ai (3–5 business days)
3. Security sign-off (SOC2 artifacts + penetration test summary) -> security@redwood.ai (3 business days)
4. Engineering packaging & integration smoke test (entitlements + metering) -> owner per-cloud (7 business days)
5. Final sign-off and submit (PMM/Partnerships)

Launch checklist (one-week countdown template)
- D-7: All copy final, assets uploaded to staging, pricing SKU assigned
- D-5: Legal + Security approvals complete
- D-3: Engineering smoke test of activation & billing callbacks (QA checklist pass)
- D-1: Marketplace listing staged and internal link shared for signoff
- D+1: Verify first activations, entitlement mapping, and basic telemetry spikes

Open questions / decisions needed
- Metering unit: Do we meter by tokens (preferred for parity with hosted billing) or by request/seat for Marketplace? (Finance + Liam)
- Private offer flow: do we publish a dedicated "Reserved Capacity" SKU or handle via Private Offer quotes only? (Sales Ops)
- Legal: are there marketplace-specific indemnity/insurance asks that differ materially from our standard contract? (Legal)
- Pricing visibility: how transparent do we want usage tiers to be in marketplace UI vs 'contact sales'?

Quick integration notes (engineering scratchpad)
- Build a small test harness that simulates marketplace activation callback (POST) to /marketplace/activate and validates entitlement ID -> tenant mapping
- Add a cloud-marketplace flag to tenant config so we can surface "marketplace origin" in billing reports
- Emit an activation event to analytics pipeline with tags: marketplace_provider, plan_sku, activation_id

Next steps & owners (immediate)
- PMM (Maya): finalize short + long copy variants and upload to shared drive (due 2026-02-28)
- Engineering (Liam/Priya/Diego): prototype entitlement activation flow + smoke test harness (due 2026-03-06)
- Legal: schedule 1:1 to review marketplace T&Cs and highlight deviations (due 2026-02-20)
- Finance: propose SKU mapping and billing metric recommendation (due 2026-02-28)

Notes to self / informal
- Keep copy density low; marketplaces prefer short bullets and clear value props.
- We will likely iterate after first AWS submission — expect small copy/audit patches.
- Slack thread: #gtm-marketplace is the fastest route for approvals; tag people in PRs.

Appendix: quick copy alternatives for CTA buttons
- "Start free" / "Try Redwood" / "Request dedicated capacity" / "Contact sales for private deployment"

Unresolved items flagged in REDW-3124.

End of playbook (working draft).
